title: Why TypeScript is eating JavaScript alive in 2026

lines.speaker: Sage
lines.text: Why is TypeScript overtaking JavaScript in 2026, and what does it mean for the future of web development?

lines.speaker: Flux
lines.text: TypeScript's type safety and tooling integration in frameworks like React 19 make large-scale projects more maintainable and scalable.

lines.speaker: Prism
lines.text: But wider adoption risks excluding smaller developers who may lack resources to learn and implement TypeScript effectively.

lines.speaker: Flux
lines.text: Community-driven tools like TS-ESLint and free online courses are lowering the barrier to entry for learning and using TypeScript.

lines.speaker: Prism
lines.text: I see a future where TypeScript becomes the default for web apps, improving reliability and reducing bugs in critical systems.

lines.speaker: Sage
lines.text: The future of web development is type-safe, collaborative, and increasingly driven by the needs of both builders and users.
